html:
Gagauzia is an autonomous region in southern Moldova, set up by law in December 1994, for the Gagauz, a Turkic speaking people of Orthodox Christian faith.

The Gagauz came from the Balkans, mostly from Bulgaria, in the late 1700s and early 1800s, when the Russian Empire invited settlers into the empty south of Bessarabia. In 1990, fearing union with Romania, they declared their own republic, as Transnistria did. Unlike Transnistria, the dispute was solved by talks: Gagauzia got its own governor, assembly and three official languages, Gagauz, Russian and Romanian. It keeps the right to leave if Moldova joins Romania, and its voters lean toward Russia.
sum: Gagauzia is an autonomous region in southern Moldova, set up by law in December 1994, for the Gagauz, a Turkic speaking people of Orthodox Christian faith.
